work_item.title: Session ownership and loop selection
work_item.description:
# Session ownership and loop selection

## Question

Is loop selection per Akh or per session, and which session properties remain stable across reconnects? Distinguish reconnecting a client, resuming a provider thread, and handing off to another loop. What are the client controller and observer rules?

## Accepted selection decision

The user chose: **“One loop fixed for each Akh.”**

Loop implementation selection belongs to the Akh configuration. All sessions
of that Akh use that implementation, with separate conversation and provider
session state. A client cannot select another loop for an individual session.
Different Akhs may use different implementations.

## Remaining lifecycle question

When changing an Akh's loop, must all its sessions be closed first?
Recommendation pending user: yes, so one Akh never has sessions running different
loop implementations at the same time. Reconnect, controller and observer rules
remain covered by the loop-contract and client-contract decisions. This ticket
remains open; its selection subdecision is accepted.

work_item.title: Codex and Claude integration contracts and subscription boundaries
work_item.description:
# Codex and Claude integration contracts and subscription boundaries

## Question

Which current official interfaces support user-owned subscription authentication, Akh custom tools, cancellation, approvals, session resume and disabling native execution? For each claim cite primary sources and version/date. Separate technical interoperability, documented support and unresolved restrictions. Can all filesystem, command, hook, MCP and subagent execution remain under Akh control without modifying provider authentication? No live model calls or credential reads are needed. Capture findings in assets/codex-claude.md.

Research branch: `research/akh-agent-loops-codex-claude`.

## Research findings available

Codex App Server and Claude SDK expose host tool callbacks. Codex hooks expressly do not form a complete execution boundary; Claude tool exclusion, strict MCP and aliases are promising but untested together. User sign-in to unmodified Claude Code and SDK product authentication have distinct published guidance. No exclusive Akh/SSH conformance claim.

[Full research asset](https://anima.wegmueller.it/documents/01a0878d-9451-7182-b97c-bf3470f924fc).

work_item.title: Cursor and OpenCode integration contracts and execution control
work_item.description:
# Cursor and OpenCode integration contracts and execution control

## Question

Which current official interfaces can implement AgentLoop for Cursor and OpenCode? Compare server/SDK, CLI, ACP, custom tools/MCP, subscription authentication, streamed events, approvals, cancellation, resume and reliable exclusion of native execution. Do not assume that supporting MCP gives full execution interception or that OpenCode can reuse another vendor subscription. Cite primary sources and explicitly record unknown capabilities. No live model calls or credential reads. Capture assets/cursor-opencode.md.

Research branch: `research/akh-agent-loops-cursor-opencode`.

## Research findings available

Cursor has ACP and an official SDK Bridge with local tool allowlisting and custom callbacks; restrictions must be reapplied on resume. OpenCode has server/ACP integration, but pinned source registers MCP by directory/name rather than session identity. Treat dedicated instances as a candidate until isolation tests pass. OpenCode documents ChatGPT access but rejects Claude subscription plugins. Neither adapter has proven exclusive Akh/SSH execution.

[Full research asset](https://anima.wegmueller.it/documents/01a0878d-94d0-7100-8258-812d3dba8eb3).

# AgentLoop contract and lifecycle events

## Question

What minimal object-safe Rust contract represents a complete loop session while leaving ChatBackend below InternalLoop and Backend below tools? Specify commands/events for start, submit, interrupt, approvals/input, finish, reconnect and close; typed outcomes/capabilities; backpressure and single-turn ownership. Account for existing synchronous tools and thread-local session context without assuming async callbacks preserve it.

# Different loop strategies and composition

## Question

How do reactive tool loops, plan-and-execute, iterative research, deterministic workflows and delegated multi-loop work fit the same session/event contract? Distinguish runtime implementation from strategy and persona. Which are InternalLoop policies versus separate AgentLoop implementors or outer coordinators? Avoid promising strategy control inside opaque provider loops or nested-loop delegation without bounded authority.
